transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
President Trump and China's leader Xi Jinping, along with some senior Chinese officials,
held much-anticipated meetings at the White House this afternoon.
NPR's Emily Fang reports the top issue for China was the island of Taiwan.
Trump and Xi met for under two hours, and they were joined by members of the U.S. Cabinet
and senior Chinese officials.
While the two delegations met in the White House, China's state news agency published
a statement on Taiwan, a Democratic island China wants control over.
The statement urges the U.S. to oppose formal Taiwan independence.
Trump had also indicated artificial intelligence would be discussed, and in his opening remarks,
Xi Jinping stressed that artificial intelligence should remain "under human control."
The two sides have also been negotiating trade and technology issues, including what the
U.S. says is a two-month extension on an agreement to access Chinese rare-earth elements.
So far, China has not confirmed the details of that extension.
Emily Fang, NPR News, Washington.
The Senate narrowly rejected a war powers resolution today.
It was the 14th time the Senate weighed in on whether to halt President Trump's war
in Iran.
More Republicans are breaking with the president over the war, which has driven the spike in
fuel prices and become a flashpoint in the midterm election.
The vote was likely to be the last chance for lawmakers to go on record about the war
ahead of November.
CNN, MS Now, and Politico say their reporters are back in the White House after being banned
by President Trump.
It comes after a federal judge temporarily blocked Trump's ban.
Trump's Justice Department lawyers cited national security as a reason for the move.
As NPR's Greg Myry explains, Trump has used the rationale multiple times.
The president's critics say he does this because judges in courts tend to be extremely
deferential when a president claims national security.
We should stress that in these recent cases, Trump didn't initially invoke national security
when he took these actions.
Only when faced with legal challenges did the president and his lawyers turn to national
security as a defense.
NPR's Greg Myry reporting, New York is suing prediction market site Poly Market, as NPR's
Bobby Allen reports state authorities say the platform is running an illegal gambling operation.
New York officials are asking a judge to push Poly Market out of the state.
Prediction markets have exploded in popularity in Trump's second term, taking in billions
of dollars in weekly bets on everything from elections to war to the word choice of politicians
and sports announcers.
More than two dozen lawsuits have been filed against the sector, which in addition to Poly
Market includes its rival, Kalshe.
Legal watchers say a case will likely eventually make its way to the Supreme Court.
In a statement, Poly Market said it will fight for its users.
The company insists it is not a gambling operator, but a company that offers a financial product
known as an events contract, something overseen by the Trump administration.
Donald Trump Jr. is a Poly Market advisor and investor.
Bobby Allen, NPR News.
U.S. stock indexes ended roughly back where they started after an up and down day today.
The S&P 500 was virtually unchanged.
This is NPR News.
A drug task force in Mississippi is urging people to avoid CRADM.
After authorities found packages of the substance while investigating the deaths of two University
of Mississippi students, CRADM is an herbal extract that can act as a stimulant or a sedative
at high doses.
It has come under scrutiny over the past decade from U.S. health officials and states.
An industry group says the FDA is conflating the natural product with synthetic and chemically
manipulated ones.
An FDA advisory panel is recommending the agency approve a blood test used to detect
multiple forms of cancer, and PRC Yuki Noguchi reports.
The gallery blood test made by the company, GRAIL, says its device can screen for up to
50 cancers using a single blood draw for those patients 50 and over.
As Michelle Tarver, head of the FDA's Center for Devices and Radiological Health, said,
"The concept of blood-based multi-cancer detection tests, such as the one being discussed
today, represents a genuinely promising opportunity.
Access to the right diagnostic test at the right time can be truly transformative.
However, at the same time, technologies with this kind of reach and novelty demand careful
rigorous evaluation."
The tests already on the market, but FDA approval, would allow Medicare to cover its cost.
Yuki Noguchi, NPR News.
American football of the gridiron variety will make its debut in Rio de Janeiro on Sunday
at a Fuji Ball Cathedral.
The 78,000-seat Maracana Stadium is a revered soccer venue that has hosted two World Cup
championship games and clashes between South America's biggest teams.
Now, the Baltimore Ravens and the Dallas Cowboys will play there.
This is NPR News from Washington.
This message comes from Charles Schwab with their original podcast, Choiceology.
Choiceology is a show about the psychology and economics behind people's decisions.
Download the latest episode and subscribe at Schwab.com/podcast.

topics.text: President Trump and China's leader Xi Jinping held White House meetings discussing Taiwan, artificial intelligence, and trade issues
Senate narrowly rejected war powers resolution on President Trump's war in Iran for the 14th time
Federal judge temporarily blocked President Trump's ban on CNN, MS Now, and Politico reporters at White House
New York suing prediction market site Poly Market, alleging it operates an illegal gambling operation
Mississippi drug task force urging people to avoid CRADM after finding it during investigation of student deaths
FDA advisory panel recommending approval of blood test by GRAIL that detects up to 50 forms of cancer
Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys to play American football at Maracana Stadium in Rio de Janeiro on Sunday
